title: Hunters in a jar

data.source: Blasius, Rudolf, Weithoff, Gaedke and Fussmann, Time series of long-term experimental predator-prey cycles, figshare, doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.10045976 (Nature 577, 2020)

prediction: Pooled over ten experiments, the correlation between one round's length and the next is above -0.25 (P1, timing errors pile up); and a higher rotifer peak is followed by a longer round (P2).
baseline: A clock with a jostled hand (correlation -0.5), pure pile-up (0), and shuffling within experiments.
why: One round's length said little about the next, so the timing errors pile up and each round starts from the last, as the grammar has it. That is also what any noisy predator-prey model does. Nothing was added.
